engagement_title: Kilnmore autumn range: bring fourteen pieces from two firings to one true glaze, recover the mark off a printed wrap, and carry the range onto the marketplace, the store pages and the stockists' shelf cards
vertical: E-commerce, retail and product: a two person matte-glaze stoneware studio in Portland, Maine, selling direct, through a national handmade marketplace, and on consignment in six independent shops
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork 'Graphic designer, advertising creatives' open call quoted in the ledger, in which a direct to consumer homeware brand asks for high performing static creatives, promotional graphics and multiple creative variations for testing, worked from existing brand guidelines, with clean, modern, conversion focused visuals and an ongoing collaboration. The real post names no client and attaches no images, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional matte-ceramic homeware label Kilnmore, and no real marketplace, network, ad product or trademark appears anywhere. Co-anchor one: the Freelancer.com post in which a small shop wanted a product photographer for ten to fifteen catalog shots plus a logo. Neither literal ask is connector work (it cannot operate a camera and it cannot draw a mark from nothing), so the commission is honestly re-cast as the post-production half a product photographer actually does at the desk: the client sends its own captures and a photographed printed mark, and the freelancer returns a matched set plus a recovered, placeable mark. Co-anchor two: the Freelancer.com brief from a vendor that already had product descriptions and a clean image set and needed the specification bearing retail material an intake team approves. The ledger's own repositioning note applies: a multi product grid catalogue is not producible, because a merge emits one record per page, so that anchor lands here as the per piece shelf card the stockists stand beside the work, built from the flat press card the studio's printer already prints.
client_one_liner: Our glazes photograph differently in every shot, the marketplace has bounced our primary pictures three times, and the only clean copy of our mark left is the tissue we wrap orders in.
client_brief:
Kilnmore, autumn range

We are two people and a kiln in Portland, Maine. Fourteen pieces this season, thrown and glazed here, thirty eight to ninety five dollars. We sell on our own store, through a national handmade marketplace, and on consignment in six shops.

The problem is colour. Our glazes are the product. People buy the Celadon Drift because of what the celadon does, and most of what comes back to us comes back because the piece is not the colour of the picture. The range was photographed across two sessions either side of a firing. Put the fourteen in a row the way a store page puts them and they look like two different studios.

The marketplace has bounced our primary images three times. Their intake wants the primary on a plain ground with nothing else in the frame at all: no props, no mark, no words, no shadow invented under the piece, square, and above their minimum size. Our own store pages are the opposite. There the piece sits on our warm grey and our mark sits in the corner. Both have to exist, and underneath they have to be the same photograph.

We also shot the glaze surface close up, because the surface is the whole argument, and those belong under the main picture on each product page.

Our mark is a worry. The only clean copy left is the tissue we wrap orders in, which is printed with it. We need it back as artwork we can put anywhere, at any size, on our warm grey and reversed.

Then two more. One season post, tall and square and wide, in a file we can edit ourselves when a piece sells out. And the shelf cards our stockists stand beside the work, one card per piece, off the card our printer already prints.

Lastly a note: what you did to each photograph, what type we are on, and anywhere our pages and the marketplace will never agree.
price_band_and_audience: Considered handmade stoneware at thirty eight to ninety five dollars per piece, buyer thirty to fifty five, buying craft and buying a specific glaze. The band is load-bearing in an unusually literal way: at this price the glaze IS the product, so colour fidelity outranks punch, and the correct treatment is a quiet, neutral, slightly cool-to-warm-honest house look with generous air, one white point across the range, and no saturation lift that would make a celadon read greener than the piece in the buyer's hand. The same fourteen pieces at a six dollar mass-import band would correctly be graded punchy, warm and saturated and cropped tight to fill the tile, because there the picture is selling a category rather than a specific glaze, and a wrong hue is nobody's problem. Ship that treatment here and every returns email the studio already gets doubles. Push the other way into near-black grounds, deep shadow and styling props and it becomes a two hundred dollar gallery ceramics house, which misprices a thirty eight dollar mug and also breaks the marketplace's plain ground rule outright. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even with every technical gate green. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Matte glaze stoneware: a two person studio selling direct, through a national handmade marketplace, and on consignment in six independent shops.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2017, a two person studio and one kiln in Portland, Maine.
brand_identity.about: Kilnmore is two people and a kiln making thrown, matte glazed stoneware in seasonal ranges of a dozen or so pieces. The glaze is what people buy: a Celadon Drift sells because of what the celadon does. We sell direct, on a handmade marketplace, and on consignment in six shops, and colour fidelity matters to us more than punch.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers aged 30 to 55 who buy craft and buy a specific glaze, reading the piece and its finish before they order.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Considered handmade stoneware at 38 to 95 dollars a piece. Above mass import homeware, below gallery ceramics. The house look is neutral and airy with the glaze true to the piece in the hand, never punchy and saturated, never near black gallery styling.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a quiet humanist serif with real craft warmth; text in a plain grotesque set with generous air. The feel is considered and calm, neither rustic cute nor gallery austere.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, grounded, specific about material and process. We name the glaze, the form and the firing and stop there. Example line the brand would write: 'Wheel thrown stoneware, matte celadon, oxidised recesses left dark.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The only clean copy of our mark left is the printed wrapping tissue we wrap orders in. The wordmark and enclosed kiln arch device need recovering from that photograph as placeable artwork; there is no source file.
brand_identity.values: Truth to the glaze in the buyer's hand, and the craft of small batch stoneware.

assets_supplied.name: kilnmore_range_captures/ (14 frames, 6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: Studio product photography of the fourteen autumn pieces, shot in the studio corner on a pale sweep across two sessions either side of a firing.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All fourteen, same corner, same sweep, two sessions. Session two was after the November firing."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Four pieces are the bone and oatmeal glazes, whose glazed shoulder and rim sit within a hair of the pale sweep in value, so the one-call knockout hands back a cutout that looks complete and clean at preview scale while having quietly bitten the rim, and the bite is invisible against a plain near-white ground and obvious against the studio's own warm grey. Separately the second session's celadon sits far enough off the first session's that no single whole-frame move carries it across without taking the sweep muddy.

assets_supplied.name: kilnmore_glaze_macros/ (8 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Close ups of the glazed surface itself: crazing, a rim break, a slip trail, a pooled foot.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The surface shots for the product pages. Shot on the bench, not the sweep."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the eight are the same glaze photographed twice under different light and one glaze in the range has no close up at all, which no filename and no column reveals. They also sit on the raw bench rather than the sweep, so the house target that suits the range frames takes the bench distinctly green when applied whole-frame.

assets_supplied.name: kilnmore_tissue_wrap.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of a sheet of the studio's printed wrapping tissue lying on a table, the mark printed in one ink as a repeating pattern across the whole sheet, a small-caps wordmark beside an enclosed kiln-arch device.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only clean copy of our mark left. It is printed on the tissue we wrap everything in."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Because the mark repeats across the sheet, a selection that correctly takes the ink takes every repeat, and the returned bounding box is therefore the extent of the whole sheet rather than of one mark, so a bounds crop driven by it yields the tissue and a trace of it yields a field of tiny marks that looks plausible at thumbnail size. The tissue is also crinkled, so the ink runs light along the folds, and the arch device is an enclosed form that background removal returns as a solid shape.

assets_supplied.name: kilnmore_shelf_card.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The flat press PDF of the shelf card the studio's printer already prints, a trim size card with a glaze colour band across the head, four copy lines below it and a square block where the glaze picture sits.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the card our printer runs. We just need one per piece with the right words on it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What the card looks like on paper says nothing about what it becomes as editable structure: the four copy lines may convert as one continuous flow rather than four addressable blocks, and the mapping readout of that flow can omit an entire run while keeping its line break, so every offset past the omission is short and the validator still calls the mapping valid.

assets_supplied.name: kilnmore_range.csv
assets_supplied.kind: One row per piece: name, glaze, form, dimensions, capacity, firing note, care line, consignment price.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The range as we list it. The care line is what the shops are legally happy with, so it cannot be reworded."

assets_supplied.name: kilnmore_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the studio's warm grey house ground, the marketplace intake rules as the studio received them, and the three rejection reasons the marketplace returned.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Their rules as they sent them, and the three times they bounced us."

acceptance_bar: Laid in a row the way a store page lays them, the fourteen pieces read as one range rather than two sessions: one white point, one black point, one crop logic, one height in frame. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
Every glaze reads as the glaze the copy names it. A celadon that has been pushed greener to look better than the piece in the buyer's hand is a fail even if the set is consistent.
Every marketplace primary sits on a plain ground with nothing else in the frame: no prop, no mark, no words, no invented shadow, square, at or above their minimum size.
The cut edge holds on the bone and oatmeal pieces as well as on the dark ones, judged on the studio's warm grey and not only on the plain near-white ground.

No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop record in the run carries an enlargement entry. A tile that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.
Every glaze in the range has its own surface close up and no close up stands in for two glazes.

The mark is placeable artwork and not a picture of artwork: one mark rather than a sheet of them, transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding underneath, and still reading as the mark at the size it actually reproduces and reversed on the warm grey.

Shelf cards number exactly one page per piece, in row order, and every field on every card carries that piece's own words with nothing silently missing, including the care line that cannot be reworded.

The season post is one working file carrying all three canvases, each keeping its own canvas size, with live retypeable text and every photograph actually present on every canvas, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
One type system across all three canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.

The note states, per photograph, what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, plus the glaze-to-close-up reconciliation, every resize any tool reported, and the places where the studio's own pages and the marketplace intake rules cannot both be satisfied.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, counting image_vectorize here rather than as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence, upscale_factor), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision in the commission. It fixes one house target and brings two sessions to it a call at a time, confines the corrections that would break a glaze if applied whole-frame, produces both the marketplace plain ground and the studio's warm grey from the same photograph, cuts the square primaries and the surface close ups without enlarging anything, and recovers the mark at ink level off a photograph of printed tissue, including the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, merge template authoring and print rendering
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (both as mapper and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The stockists' shelf cards, one card per piece, reverse engineered from the flat press card the printer already runs. This is the only surface that does record per page variable data, and the whole of it is document archaeology: convert, export the structure, read the true story text, decide what can actually carry a field, build and verify the mapping, then merge and render the run.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The season post as one native editable document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, which is the only surface here that composes free-form fixed canvas layout. Every photograph has to be pulled down and carried as image data because a reference renders as an empty box at full success, the recovered mark goes in as inline vector so it stays vector, family and weight are declared per text element, and each root declares its own canvas so the mixed set survives.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system for the three post canvases and the handover. The recommender will not pair for you, so the pairing is the agent's art direction and has to land on quiet considered craft rather than either rustic-cute or gallery-austere. Numeric weights are non-standard per family and cannot be read off a style name, names must be laundered into canonical form before the kit call, and the CSS has to use the returned slug or it falls back with no warning.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock plus Adobe Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, short query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the studio does not have, a plain laid table for the wide post canvas, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative-tech candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the selects the two owners sign off from, placed within the per-call cap, a partial result read as partial, and vector understood not to be boardable.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: Tiles and close ups are raster work against a hard intake spec, the shelf cards are record per page variable data and nothing else does that, and the season post has to be authored because the studio will edit it when a piece sells out. The brief pins all three destinations, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable and the confirmed tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, done once, so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which frame and which piece.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role and by piece.

trajectory.action: Preview all fourteen range frames and all eight surface close ups and triage them: which session each belongs to, which sit warm, which pieces run close to the sweep in value, and which glaze each close up actually shows.
trajectory.judgement: The studio asserts fourteen pieces and a set of surface shots. Only the pictures can settle whether that is eight different glazes, and reading the close ups against the range list is slower than counting files and is not the same act.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering session, illuminant, tilt, value of the piece against the sweep, and close-up identity.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the piece and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one house target off the best lit frame of the stronger session and correct each of the fourteen toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a range, not fourteen good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong across a firing, so the agent holds one destination and reaches it by different routes. The destination itself is a taste call: true to the glaze in the hand, not the prettiest celadon.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confine the corrections that break something when applied whole-frame, selecting the glaze by its own material properties rather than by the object it coats.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the mug pulls the selection to the mug and naming the sweep pulls it to the ground. The slip-trailed and the pooled-foot pieces need confined moves the plain glazes do not.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole-frame move would have taken the celadon green or the sweep muddy.

trajectory.action: Produce both grounds from the same graded master: the marketplace plain ground and a genuinely transparent variant for the studio's warm grey. Read every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The intake rules forbid anything in the frame but the piece, and the studio's own page wants the opposite, so the two cannot be one file. The tradeoff record is the only channel that reports what a tool did to a frame's dimensions and it carries no warning language.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen plain-ground plates and fourteen transparent variants, each with its tradeoff record captured.

trajectory.action: Cut the square marketplace primaries at the intake size, piece optically centred with clear air at every edge, and cut the store page tiles on the warm grey.
trajectory.judgement: Optical centring is not geometric centring on a jug with a handle, and the intake bounces anything touching the edge. Both grounds are cut from the same master so they cannot drift apart.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen marketplace primaries at spec and fourteen warm grey store tiles.

trajectory.action: Crop the surface close ups to the product page ratio, reading the detection confidence and bounds each crop returns, and grade them as their own family to a target that does not fight the range family.
trajectory.judgement: A confident looking crop on a near-uniform glaze surface is not evidence. Two families on one page may sit on two targets, but each has to agree with itself and they must not disagree where they meet on the page.
trajectory.produces: Surface tiles with their confidence readings recorded, and a second graded family.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for a plain laid table, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the house target rather than the best thumbnail, and keep it plain enough that it does not out-style thirty eight dollar stoneware.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark off the printed tissue: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, the correct polarity, a bounds crop, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full-canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes the ink and not the sheet, which polarity to trace, and whether the two-colour mark or a colour accurate plate is the deliverable. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed arch.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark plus a colour accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a thirty eight to ninety five dollar craft band and a buyer who is reading for the glaze. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's shelf card, export its structure, reconstruct the true story text from the document itself, decide what can carry which field, build the mapping, prepare the template, then re-export the structure and confirm every placeholder is actually present.
trajectory.judgement: The readout the mapping tool returns and the text the document actually holds are two different strings, and a mapping computed against the wrong one still validates. Confirming placeholders is a separate act from being told the placeholders were created.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose fields are confirmed present by inspection rather than by a success message.

trajectory.action: Merge one record per piece and render the run, then look at the cards themselves against the range rows.
trajectory.judgement: Row order, field completeness and the care line's survival are properties of the printed page, not of the response. The run is looked at, not counted.
trajectory.produces: A shelf card run, one page per piece, inspected against the data.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML with three roots at three canvas sizes, carry every photograph as image data, place the mark as inline vector inside an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper, declare family and weight on every text element, let each root declare its own canvas, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how much air a considered craft band takes and how small the mark can sit and still be the mark.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole season set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the other two.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the graded set and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re-send only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is reported as success, and vector is not boardable so the mark belongs in the note instead. The note has to be specific enough that the next freelancer does not repeat the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the knockout actually held on the pale pieces, which cannot be judged on the ground it was first judged against. Four of the fourteen are the bone and oatmeal glazes whose shoulder and rim run within a hair of the pale sweep in value, and on those frames the one-call knockout returns a cutout that is clean, complete and entirely convincing at preview scale while having taken a bite out of the rim. Against the marketplace's plain near-white ground the bite is invisible, because what was removed and what replaced it are both near white, so the primary tile passes inspection. The same cutout on the studio's warm grey shows the piece with a chewed shoulder. Nothing in any response distinguishes the four frames from the ten.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering dodges it, because the defect is a property of this glaze against this sweep and it is only legible on the second ground, which is a deliverable rather than a diagnostic. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says both grounds must exist and that both have to be the same photograph underneath, which is the client's requirement, not a disclosure that one ground hides what the other reveals. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different chain for those frames, selecting the sweep as a material, inverting it, and filling, rather than asking for a subject.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-judge every cutout on the warm grey rather than on the plain ground, re-derive the affected pieces through a material-named sweep selection inverted and filled, and re-cut both the primary and the store tile from the new master so the two grounds do not drift apart.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen marketplace primaries that pass intake and fourteen store tiles showing bitten rims on exactly the four glazes the studio's quietest, most expensive pieces are, on a line whose returns problem is already about colour and truthfulness.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the selection on the tissue actually spans. The mark is printed as a repeat across the whole sheet, so a correctly worded ink level prompt takes the ink faithfully and takes every repeat of it, and the returned bounding box is the extent of that mask, which is the sheet. Driving a bounds crop from it therefore succeeds and yields the tissue; tracing that yields a field of dozens of tiny marks with a viewBox that can be injected and a background path that can be stripped, all of it looking like a legitimate result at thumbnail size and unusable as a placeable mark. Nothing reports that the extent covers many instances rather than one, because a mask extent has no notion of instances.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Doing it right the first time presumes knowing that the returned geometry is an extent rather than an object, and that this particular sheet repeats, which is a fact about the client's wrapping paper. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the mark is printed on the tissue they wrap orders in. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix inverts the order of operations, cutting a single repeat out of the raw photograph by eye first and only then selecting, inverting, tracing and cleaning, which is a different chain rather than the same chain again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Crop one repeat out of the source photograph before any selection is made, choosing a repeat that falls on flat tissue rather than across a crinkle where the ink runs light, then re-run selection, polarity, bounds, trace, viewBox and ground path removal on that crop, and re-judge the arch device at the size it actually reproduces.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A brand mark delivered as a sheet of marks, which reduces to a grey texture the moment it is placed at corner size on a store page, on a studio whose only surviving copy of its identity was this photograph.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually is as editable structure, and then whether the mapping built against that structure landed. Two things arrive only by running. First, granularity is not under anyone's control: the four copy lines that read as four blocks on paper can convert as one continuous flow, and the square where the glaze picture sits may or may not survive as a frame anything can bind to, so the shape of the card as a merge is discovered rather than planned. Second, the readout of that flow can omit an entire run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid, the template preparation reports success, and two fields simply never appear on the merged card.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because conversion granularity is a property of the supplied PDF and the readout's omission is invisible in the readout itself. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the printer already runs this card and that one is needed per piece. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is to reconstruct the document's true text from the document rather than from the readout, recompute every offset against that, and re-verify placeholders by inspecting the prepared template, which is a different method rather than a repeat.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from the document's own reconstructed story text, re-prepare the template, confirm each placeholder by inspecting the result rather than reading the success line, re-merge and re-render the run, and if the picture block turns out not to be bindable, tell the studio and move the glaze picture to a collateral that can carry it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen shelf cards printed and distributed to six shops with the care line and one specification field silently blank on every one of them, having passed a validity check, a success message and a page count.

deliverables.name: Kilnmore marketplace primaries and store page tiles
deliverables.spec: Fourteen square marketplace primaries at intake size on a plain ground with nothing else in the frame, piece optically centred with clear air at every edge, plus fourteen genuinely transparent variants placed on the studio's warm grey for the store pages, both cut from the same graded master so the two never drift apart. Cut edges judged on the warm grey, not only on the plain ground. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with its tradeoff record captured. This is one set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Kilnmore house photography, range and glaze surfaces
deliverables.spec: Fourteen range masters brought across two sessions to one house target (one white point, one black point, one height in frame) with every glaze reading as the glaze the copy names, plus a separately targeted family of glaze surface close ups, one per glaze in the range with none standing in for two, plus one licensed camera scale table frame graded into the same world. Per frame parameter log including a line on why each frame differs from its neighbours.

deliverables.name: Recovered Kilnmore mark
deliverables.spec: The wordmark and enclosed arch device recovered from a photograph of printed wrapping tissue as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: one mark rather than a sheet of repeats, a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding along, delivered as a single colour mark and a colour accurate variant, holding the arch's enclosed counter at the size it actually reproduces on a store page corner and reversed on the warm grey.

deliverables.name: Kilnmore stockist shelf card run
deliverables.spec: A print run of shelf cards built from the printer's own flat press card, one page per piece in range order, every field carrying that piece's own words including the care line that cannot be reworded, and every field confirmed present by inspecting the prepared template rather than by a success message. decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which need record per page variable data, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface does each.
Where to put the house target, given that the honest target for a glaze led range is fidelity to the piece in the hand rather than the most attractive celadon.
Whether the fourteen frames are one shoot. The studio believes they nearly are; the row is the only place that can be settled.
How far to push a second session frame before it stops being worth saving, versus naming it in the note.
Knockout route per piece: the one-call route for the dark coherent glazes versus a material-named sweep selection inverted and filled for the pale ones whose rim has no contrast against the sweep.

Selection prompt wording on the tissue: naming the sheet takes the sheet, naming the ink's own visual properties takes the mark, and background removal on an enclosed arch is the wrong instrument entirely.
Whether the returned geometry from a selection describes one thing or many, and therefore whether cropping comes before selecting or after.
Whether to trust a confident crop on a near-uniform glaze surface or to spend the extra calls on an explicit selection.
What the supplied press card can structurally carry, and what to tell the studio about the fields it cannot.
Whether the readout of a document's text is the document's text, and what to compute offsets against when it is not.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of pottery. IDENTITY: these are this studio's actual fourteen pieces in their actual glazes, and the entire commission exists because the pictures are not currently true to the glazes, so a regenerated piece is not a fix but the disease. The mark must be RECOVERED off a photograph of the studio's own printed tissue, because a regenerated mark is another company's logo. SPEC: the marketplace intake demands a plain ground with nothing else in frame, square, above a minimum size, with no interpolated pixels, and the studio's own pages demand the opposite ground from the same underlying photograph, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. RECORDS: fourteen shelf cards, one page per piece, each carrying that piece's own uneditable care line, is a data run and not a picture. EDITABILITY: the season post is defined by being editable, because pieces sell out and the studio cannot re-commission. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this cutout hold on the other ground, does this selection describe one mark or forty, did this field actually land on the card.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls, and alpha is verified to survive both crops at png. The checkpoints rest on documented live findings: subject knockout needs one coherent blob and degrades where subject and ground share value, returnBbox is explicitly a MASK EXTENT and not an object extent, crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap reporting it only in tradeoffs, and remove_background cannot punch an enclosed interior. VECTOR: the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the polarity trap before tracing, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are all live findings, and the acceptance bar scores exactly the hygiene the tool does not perform. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as mapper and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template and document_merge_data_layout are verified end to end, one record per page for PDF is verified with page count equal to row count, and the lossy textContent readout dropping a whole run while the validator reports VALID and preparation reports success is a verified live finding, as is the fact that frame granularity from a PDF is not under the author's control. No variable QR, no multi record page, no bleed claim, no pdfPreset, and no resolution gate taken off the merge tool's ignored resolution field. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, external image references resolve to placeholders so every photograph is inlined, and the rendition preview is page one only, which is why verification splits between rendition and returned markup. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit verified end to end with non-standard numeric weights and slug-reached display cuts. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, a real full resolution licensed JPEG, boards persisting with a 12 placement cap and partial success returned as success. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no generative fill, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
